newsitem.title: MEXICO: Analysts applaud Mexico's good March trade number.
newsitem.headline: Analysts applaud Mexico's good March trade number.

text.p: Mexico's trade surplus was bouyed in March as growth in imports was outpaced by export growth, defying expectations that the surplus would weaken as the year wears on, economists said on Wednesday.

"It is surprising. There have been concerns the monthly trade surplus would decline for some time," said James Carlen, American Express Financial Services director of economic analysis for emerging markets.
The Finance Ministry said on Wednesday the preliminary trade surplus in March was $565 million, on exports of $8.732 billion and imports of $8.167 billion.
A Reuters survey of economists in 11 brokerage houses, banks and research firms had found expectations of a surplus of $324.29 million, with exports of $8.74 billion and imports of $8.41 billion.
In February the revised trade surplus was $323 million, up from a preliminary figure of $264 million. Exports in February were $8.008 billion, while imports were $7.685 billion.
Many analysts had expected the trade surplus to decline during the year as a strong peso cut into exports and increased imports.
But the peso has refused to weaken substantially and exports have remained strong.

"What we are seeing now is that despite a strong peso and the U.S. interest rate hike, we are still seeing strong export growth, even as internal absorption is growing," said Scott Grimberg, an economist with MMS International said.
He said the continued strength in the U.S. economy, Mexico's largest export market, has helped keep Mexico's exports robust.
Analysts said the good trade surplus number in March will be supportive for the peso.
The strong surplus removes one possible catalyst for a weakening of the Mexican currency, they said.
In January the surplus was $460 million.
